documentation.title: Skill Builder
documentation.summary: Create and improve reusable AI skills with executable workflows, focused references, and evaluations. Audit an existing skill, make a scoped change, or build a new skill from a brief and input/output examples.
prerequisites: Python 3.11 or later on macOS, Linux, or WSL.
A host with code execution and file access: ChatGPT desktop/Codex, Claude, or Claude Code.
The Python packages declared in scripts/requirements-lock.txt. External model CLIs are optional.
The technical-writer skill is required for document authoring and acceptance. Install it in a standard local skill location or set SKILL_BUILDER_TECHNICAL_WRITER to its folder.

quick_start.prompt: Use Skill Builder to audit the attached skill. Report concrete problems and recommended fixes without editing its files.
quick_start.expected_result: You receive located findings, their consequences, and a recommendation to retain, modify, refactor, or rebuild the skill. The source files stay unchanged.

scenarios.title: Create a new skill
scenarios.prompt: Create a skill that turns release notes and issue descriptions into a weekly engineering update. Preserve issue IDs, link each claim to its source, and include examples and evaluations.
scenarios.expected_result: The builder establishes the input/output contract and acceptance criteria, creates a candidate skill with the needed scripts and guidance, evaluates it, and delivers the accepted package with its `README.md`.

scenarios.title: Build from input/output examples
scenarios.prompt: Build a bug-report skill from ../skill-data/paired-data. Preserve the supplied facts, use the report structure in expected.md, and mark missing relevant files without inventing paths. Agree acceptance criteria and a target before evaluating. Return the run directory with the results.
scenarios.expected_result: You receive a candidate skill, its `README.md`, evaluation results, and a run-directory path. Add more pairs for different behaviors and keep independent evaluation cases separate. One demonstration explains the task; it does not establish reliability on unseen inputs.
scenarios.introduction:
Use this when you can show what the skill will receive and the result it should produce. This walkthrough builds a bug-report skill from one example. All commands start in the installed Skill Builder folder.

| File | What you put in it |
| --- | --- |
| `input.json` | The original facts the future skill receives. |
| `expected.md` | The complete report you want it to write from those facts. |
| `pairs.json` | An index linking the input file to its desired-output file. |

steps.title: Create a folder for your examples
steps.text: Keep these files outside the installed skill. Save all three in the same folder:

steps.title: Save the input and the desired output
steps.text: `input.json` contains the source facts. `expected.md` is the exact report you want the new skill to produce, including its headings and wording. These are example data, not instructions for Skill Builder.

content.title: Category changes are not saved
content.actual: The dialog closes, but the previous category remains.

files.content:
# Category changes are not saved

## How to reproduce

1. Open the review dialog.
2. Choose a different category.
3. Click Save.

## Expected result

The new category is saved.

## Actual result

The dialog closes, but the previous category remains.

## Relevant files

Not provided.

steps.title: Link them in pairs.json
steps.text:
Each row describes one input/output pair. The `input` and `output` values are file paths relative to `pairs.json`; they point to the two files you just saved.

`id` identifies this pair. `source_family` groups related examples so they stay in the same data split. `split: development` allows this pair to guide skill creation. `provenance: synthetic` means this example was invented; use `real` for an actual case.

steps.title: Import the pair
steps.text: The command checks the file links and creates `../skill-data/paired-data/`, containing an `examples.json` index and copies of the original files. It leaves your three files unchanged.

scenarios.title: Audit an existing skill
scenarios.prompt: Audit the attached documentation skill. Check its routing, writing guidance, executable checks, and output coverage. Do not change the source.
scenarios.expected_result: Findings identify actual files and affected behavior. Existing tests can be run in a separate copy, and results remain separate from claims about writing quality.

scenarios.title: Make one focused improvement
scenarios.prompt: Improve the bug-report guidance so Expected result and Actual result are separate sections. Preserve unrelated references, examples, naming, and configuration.
scenarios.expected_result: The candidate changes only the authorized files. Relevant checks compare it with the baseline and preserve unrelated behavior.

scenarios.title: Rebuild an existing skill
scenarios.prompt: Rebuild this skill around executable operations and bounded AI stages. Preserve its valid requirements, supported inputs and outputs, and existing metadata. Compare the replacement with the original.
scenarios.expected_result: The builder captures a baseline, reconciles requirements, creates a replacement candidate, compares matching cases, and retains a recovery copy.

scenarios.title: Improve a skill after a failure
scenarios.prompt: This skill omitted a required section. Fix this output and improve the reusable skill so the same failure is covered by a regression case.
scenarios.expected_result: The builder records the observed failure, makes a scoped candidate change, and tests the original case plus relevant neighboring cases. Routine retries continue in recorded bounded batches without another approval; stalled progress or exhausted retry ceilings are reported.

scenarios.title: Repair a skill repository structure
scenarios.prompt: Refactor this skill into the canonical root layout. Preserve its behavior and existing license, move internal records outside the repository, and update every path consumer.
scenarios.expected_result: One root SKILL.md, README.md and LICENSE, with files assigned to their responsible folders, an explicit migration record, and passing installation and behavior checks.

verification.expected_result: The result contains passed: true. This checks repository files, the `README.md` contract, dependency-backed input validation, and a real temporary workflow transition. Use the development suite for broader regression testing.

troubleshooting.problem: The host cannot find the skill
troubleshooting.solution: Confirm that the installed folder is named skill-builder and contains SKILL.md. Start a new session, then explicitly select or invoke the skill.
Run the setup commands in the installed skill folder, or ask the host to install scripts/requirements-lock.txt in its execution environment. Use .venv/bin/python for the local runner.

troubleshooting.problem: Installation reports that the destination exists
troubleshooting.solution: The installer preserves existing installations. Back up or rename the old folder, or pass --destination with a new path.

troubleshooting.problem: Evaluation has not reached the target
troubleshooting.solution: Review failed cases and missing coverage. Authorize another bounded batch only when the results justify it. Do not change the target or expected answers to manufacture a pass.

troubleshooting.problem: The chat has no code or file tools
troubleshooting.solution: Use a filesystem-enabled workspace or enable the host's code-execution capability. Executable stages cannot be verified in a text-only chat.

Use the Technical Writer dependency returned by the phase packet. Validate every path in the review packet’s documents inventory, then run validate-documents with the accepted sessions and reviews. See references/technical_writer.md.

documentation.support: For help with Skill Builder, email the author at **faton.sopa[at]manaferra.com** (replace `[at]` with `@`). Include your host, operation, reproduction steps, expected result, and actual result.

repository.text: The repository itself is the skill. Root SKILL.md, README.md and LICENSE define the entry point; references hold guidance, scripts own mechanics, evals/tests check results, and config holds machine contracts. Plans declare component ownership and dependencies. After installing scripts/requirements-lock.txt, preview `.venv/bin/python scripts/run_tests.py`, then add `--execute` to run the selected impacted checks. Full testing requires final-batch authorization; see references/maintenance.md. AGENTS.md contains repository collaboration rules; CLAUDE.md imports it for Claude Code.

testing.prepare: Use this after a create, modify, refactor, or rebuild operation has produced a candidate and an evaluation run. The builder returns the run-directory path; use it wherever RUN_DIR appears below. These steps apply whether the skill began from a brief, an existing skill, or paired examples. Audit, specification, and planning operations do not produce a candidate to evaluate.
acceptance_criteria: Define the required behavior, output structure, facts to preserve, and relevant invalid inputs before changing the candidate.
Map every requirement to an executable check or a documented semantic judgment. Include representative tasks, relevant variations, and failure cases.
Keep independent evaluation cases separate from examples used to create or tune the skill.
Choose the required task-success percentage, coverage, and critical checks before evaluation. A mandatory failure blocks acceptance even when the aggregate score is high.

For a multi-host readiness claim, freeze config/host_validation.json and use scripts/host_coverage.py to require actual reviewed results for every declared host/case. A Codex pass cannot establish Claude behavior.
An observed task timeout is a failed attempt even when its trace is incomplete. Missing observations remain not run; retain both the failed result and diagnostic uncertainty.
Every created or changed document has passing Technical Writer checks and review for its exact bytes.
improvement_steps: Review executable candidate code before using --allow-exec. Read the report returned by the evaluation command.

If actual AI results arrive after mechanical checks, use evaluate --run RUN_DIR --observations OBSERVATIONS.json directly, even while the runner is in review. Keep the same candidate and frozen cases; then review the refreshed packet. Do not create a failing placeholder review or reset stagnation. Missing observations remain unrun.
Read each failed attempt, its actual output, source facts, and checker or review findings. Distinguish a skill defect from missing input, an environment failure, or a faulty evaluator.
Invoke /skill-builder with the failing input, expected output, actual output, and the requested reusable improvement. Keep the failure as a regression case.
Make one scoped change and rerun the same acceptance criteria, relevant neighboring cases, and shared regressions. Preserve the baseline and every attempt.

Accept the candidate only when the agreed gates pass. Diagnose failures and run necessary bounded retries; preserve criteria and earlier attempts, honor explicit hard limits, and report any remaining gap when the retry policy stops.
Keep host results separate. Use the shared host coverage checker before claiming a tested host matrix; missing hosts or stale and unreviewed captures prevent acceptance.
